chapter: Arranging for Fletcher, Goodman and Barnet
title: Writing for Jimmy Dorsey: write only when you feel like it
summary: Horace compares wealthy Barnet's demands with Jimmy Dorsey, who told him to write only when he felt like it and paid him anyway.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: That's a big group, and I had to make two arrangements a week. This was in the contract. This was rough, but I never got a chance to go anywhere. (Inaudible). Now I did a little writing for Jimmy Dorsey, too. Now the difference between he and Charley -- and God knows Charley could have stood this better than Jimmy, because Charley's family was wealthy and so was Charlie, you know, and what he cared about a dollar was less. He wasn't cheap at all, but he wanted those two arrangements a week. Jimmy Dorsey was just the opposite. Now I stayed with Jimmy for a few months, but Jimmy always told me this: "Horace, if you feel like writing, you write. If you don't, don't do it because whichever you write, your mood's gonna be on that paper." I thought that was great, you know. And sure enough, it was like that way sometimes. You didn't feel good and you'd write and it wasn't up to par, you know, and he'd still pay you.
Jimmy Dorsey. He would still pay you.
In other words, you were salaried with him also.
Yes. Yes, I was with Jimmy -- not so long as Charley Barnet, but I had a lot of fun with him.
